topics.name: Consumer rights
topics.example: An online seller won't refund a defective product. What can I do?
topics.title: A starting point for your consumer complaint
topics.intro: You can raise a consumer grievance through the National Consumer Helpline (NCH). Whether a refund or another remedy is available depends on the facts of your purchase.

facts.text: NCH helps with consumer grievances before litigation. It is a complaint resolution service, and submitting a grievance does not guarantee a remedy.
Register through the NCH portal or call 1915. The published call hours are 8 AM–8 PM, excluding national holidays.
If the grievance remains unresolved, you can consider approaching the appropriate Consumer Commission. NCH is separate from that formal process.
NCH gives a unique docket number for a registered grievance. Use the portal's Track your Grievance option to check its status.

steps: As a practical preparation step, keep the invoice, order details, photos and correspondence together.
Describe what happened and the remedy you are requesting in your NCH grievance.
Save the grievance docket number so you can follow up.
topics.caveat: This guide does not determine your right to a refund, filing deadline, or the correct Consumer Commission for your case.
followUps: How do I track my consumer complaint?

topics.name: Cyber fraud
topics.example: I lost money in a UPI scam. Where should I report it?
topics.title: Report suspected financial cyber fraud promptly
topics.intro: If money was lost in an online scam, act promptly. Reporting gives the authorities a record; it does not guarantee recovery.

facts.text: I4C advises reporting cyber fraud immediately by calling 1930 or using the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal.
The National Consumer Helpline also directs financial cyber fraud complaints to 1930.

steps: Call 1930 and follow the reporting instructions, or visit cybercrime.gov.in.
As practical preparation, preserve transaction references, timestamps and messages. Do not send them to this chatbot.
Contact your bank through its official channel to report the transaction and ask about protecting your account.
topics.caveat: This guide cannot freeze a transfer, file a report, or promise that money will be recovered. Never share an OTP, PIN or password here.

topics.name: Free legal aid
topics.example: I cannot afford a lawyer. Can I get free legal aid?
topics.title: Explore free legal aid through NALSA
topics.intro: Legal Services Authorities can help eligible people with legal assistance. The relevant authority will assess your application and situation.

facts.text: Eligibility categories include women, children, members of Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes, people with disabilities, industrial workmen and people in custody. There are other categories too.
Income-based eligibility depends on the applicable state rules and court. There is no single income threshold that works for every case across India.
Call the national legal aid helpline 15100 or approach a Legal Services Authority. Applications can also be made on plain paper; legal aid clinics can assist.

steps: Contact 15100 or the District Legal Services Authority at your district court.
Ask which eligibility category and supporting documents apply to you.
Prepare a short account of your issue, relevant dates and any notices for the authority.
topics.caveat: This is an introduction to applying, not an eligibility decision. Avoid posting identity documents or financial records in chat.
followUps: Are women eligible regardless of income?

topics.name: Support for women
topics.example: Can a woman get free legal aid even if she earns an income?
topics.title: Free legal assistance for women
topics.intro: You can contact a Legal Services Authority to discuss your situation and understand the legal options that may apply.

facts.text: NALSA states that a woman is eligible to apply for free legal aid irrespective of her income or financial status under Section 12(c) of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
NALSA lists district, state and taluk legal services institutions, legal aid clinics and the 15100 helpline as routes to assistance.
After applying, retain the diary number provided to track your application and follow up with the relevant authority.

steps: If you are in immediate danger, call 112 when it is safe to do so.
For legal assistance, contact 15100 or visit a District Legal Services Authority.
Ask a panel lawyer or paralegal volunteer for help with the application.
topics.caveat: This guide does not assess a specific offence or choose a legal remedy for you. A legal aid lawyer can review your circumstances.

topics.name: Right to information
topics.example: How do I file an RTI request for central government information?
topics.title: Start an RTI request with the correct authority
topics.intro: The RTI Online portal provides a route to request information from the central public authorities listed on it.

facts.text: This portal is for central government public authorities. State government requests, including NCT of Delhi requests, should not be filed through it.
The portal requires the prescribed application fee for non-BPL applicants. BPL applicants are exempt when they attach the required certificate.
Keep your registration number to check status. The portal also provides a first-appeal option, for which its FAQ states there is no fee.

steps: Identify which public authority holds the records and whether it is central or state-level.
For a listed central authority, use Submit Request on the official RTI portal.
State the records you seek clearly and keep the registration details.
topics.caveat: This short guide does not cover exemptions, appeal deadlines or state-specific filing rules. Check the current official instructions before submitting.
followUps: Can I use this RTI portal for a state government?

topics.name: Urgent help
topics.example: I am in immediate danger. Where can I get urgent help?
topics.title: Your immediate safety comes first
topics.intro: If there is immediate danger, contact emergency services as soon as it is safe to do so. This chat cannot contact responders for you.

facts.text: 112 is India's unified emergency number for assistance with emergencies, including police, health and fire services.

steps: Call 112 when safe, and tell the responder where you are and what is happening.
If possible, move to a safer place and seek help from someone you trust.
topics.caveat: Do not wait for a chatbot answer when urgent assistance is needed.
